digest.en: Tech market sell-offs deepen as US inflation fears collide with AI debt. Meanwhile, Zelensky vows refinery strikes while expressing anger at US intelligence disruption. The geopolitical and financial fronts are tightening simultaneously.

articles.title: 10 years of The Coconut Club: How its S$12.80 nasi lemak challenged the way we value local food
articles.summary: The Coconut Club marked its tenth anniversary in Singapore. The restaurant serves nasi lemak for S$12.80. This price point challenged local norms for traditional food. The owner used an F1 engineer to build a cold-press coconut machine. Staff inspect daily batches of ikan bilis for quality. The decade-long operation focused on specific, high-cost production methods. This approach redefined the perceived value of local dishes. The business model prioritized ingredient sourcing over volume. The restaurant demonstrated that premium pricing could apply to everyday meals.

articles.title: ‘AI lowers the capital needed’: India’s drug discovery push faces test of human trials
articles.summary: Indian biopharmaceutical firms use artificial intelligence to identify drug candidates faster and cheaper. However, industry experts warn the technology only addresses part of the lengthy development process. Human trials remain the critical bottleneck for these AI-assisted discoveries. Indian scientists and biopharmaceutical firms are using artificial intelligence to identify promising drug candidates faster and at lower cost. But industry experts tell CNA the technology can address only part of a lengthy and risky development process.

articles.title: Attacking Trump, Zelensky showed lack of judgment
articles.summary: Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Donald Trump after Ukraine struck two Russian oil refineries. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Aleksandr Novak confirmed the attacks on the facilities. Zelensky had previously thwarted a US request to avoid targeting Russian energy infrastructure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s harsh words about US President Donald Trump were an emotional response after Zelensky deliberately thwarted Trump’s request that Ukraine not strike Russian refineries.

articles.title: Milei adviser claims UK being ‘colonised by Islam’ as Falklands row grows
articles.summary: Santiago Caputo, adviser to Argentine President Milei, claimed the UK is being colonized by Islam. He cited the election of MP Sagal Abdi-Wali as evidence. The post supports Argentina's push for sovereignty over the Falkland Islands. articles.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
articles.summary: Global tech markets suffered a deep sell-off driven by inflation fears and AI sector debt. Shares in Samsung and SoftBank plunged as traders worried about potential interest rate hikes. The decline reflects growing anxiety over the heavy borrowing underpinning current artificial intelligence infrastructure. Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook marketsBusiness news – live updatesLarry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
articles.summary: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity. A global hunger monitor report released Thursday confirmed these are the highest levels ever recorded. Conditions are expected to worsen significantly in the coming months due to ongoing rights violations. Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

articles.title: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags
articles.summary: The UN warns fewer than half of national biodiversity targets are on track. This report arrives days before the COP17 conference in Yerevan, Armenia. The assessment highlights a significant gap in global efforts to protect plants, animals, and ecosystems from further degradation. Fewer than half of the national targets set to protect the world’s plants, animals and ecosystems are on track, the UN warns in a new report, days before countries gather in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.

articles.title: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns
articles.summary: A new UN report warns rapid transitions in AI, green energy, and demographics risk deepening inequalities. These shifts are reshaping economies worldwide while creating new opportunities. Vulnerable communities face the greatest threat of being left behind by these structural changes. Rapid transformations – from artificial intelligence and digital technologies to renewable energy and demographic shifts – are reshaping economies worldwide, creating new opportunities but also threatening to deepen socio-economic inequalities, a new UN report warned on Thursday.

articles.title: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology
articles.summary: A new UN report warns that neurotechnology is outpacing human rights protections. Brain signals from gaming headsets or wellness gadgets could potentially be used as evidence against individuals in court. The report calls for limits on the use of such data. Brain signals recorded by a gaming headset or a wellness gadget could one day be used as evidence against you in court, according to a new UN report which warns that neurotechnology is outpacing the laws meant to protect human rights.

articles.title: WHO urges faster action to end lead exposure which kills 3.5 million annually
articles.summary: The World Health Organization urged countries to accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure. The toxic metal causes more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year. It also affects hundreds of millions of children worldwide. Countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure, which is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Thursday.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Vows Refinery Strikes, Expresses Anger At US Intel Disruption
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the resumption of attacks on Russian energy facilities. He also expressed anger over a dangerous disruption of US satellite intelligence that hindered Ukrainian operations. Ukrainian forces have struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, Russian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would resume attacks on Russian energy facilities and voiced anger over a "dangerous" disruption of satellite intelligence from the United States.

articles.title: US banks on bunker-busting Tomahawks to crack China’s missile wall
articles.summary: The US Navy plans to award Raytheon a sole-source contract for bunker-busting Tomahawk missiles. The move aims to counter deeply buried missile sites protected by robust air defenses. However, the system faces significant logistical and escalation challenges if deployed against China. The US Navy’s bunker-busting Tomahawk push reflects growing recognition from the Iran war that striking deeply buried missile sites protected by robust air defenses requires long-range standoff weapons.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
articles.summary: Senegal authorities detained more than 320 LGBTQ+ individuals since February after the government tightened its law criminalising homosexuality. The arrests triggered forced HIV testing and limited access to legal representation, according to a Human Rights Watch report. The crackdown signals a broader clamp At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reportsMass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report. articles.title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region
articles.summary: Indonesia is testing dry ice dispersal in South Sumatra. The government deployed planes to combat toxic haze. This follows failed cloud seeding attempts. Regional neighbors remain angry over the smoke. Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South SumatraAs fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice. Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fire.

articles.title: Ukrainian gain on a drone-filled battlefield
articles.summary: Ukraine announced Operation Vivaldi in mid-September. Forces retaken territory near Lyman. The offensive disrupted Russian advances. Gains remain limited despite heavy drone activity. Russia’s drone and missile attacks on Ukraine’s population and infrastructure continue to dominate coverage of the conflict. But on the ground, Ukraine has been making significant, if still limited, gains. articles.title: Girls In Hijabs Turned Away From Azerbaijani Schools Amid Protests Over Dress Code
articles.summary: Azerbaijani parents and students protested after schools barred girls wearing hijabs from classes. The dispute followed a new ban on clothing deemed incompatible with secular education. The move has intensified friction between religious families and state policy. A new dress-code dispute in Azerbaijan’s public schools has sparked protests by parents and students after reports that girls wearing hijabs, or Islamic headscarf, were turned away from classes.

articles.title: Ukraine Tests AI-Powered Drones As Debate Grows Over Autonomous Weapons
articles.summary: Ukraine is deploying artificial intelligence in drones to track and engage targets. Military officials confirm humans retain control over lethal decisions. Developers caution that fully autonomous weapons systems are approaching operational reality on the battlefield. Ukraine is increasingly using artificial intelligence in drones and other battlefield systems to track, identify, and attack targets. Military officials say humans still remain in control of lethal decisions, but developers warn that fully autonomous weapons are moving closer to reality.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau's health minister stated the government did not authorize a Danish-led hepatitis B trial in newborns. The study, backed by the US government and private partners, would not test vaccine safety or effectiveness. The ministry denied approval for the controversial research. Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK JrGuinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday. articles.title: EU Working On Multiple Fronts To Limit Russians From Entering Bloc
articles.summary: The European Union is developing measures to restrict Russian citizens from entering the bloc. Officials are considering a total ban on non-essential travel into the Schengen zone. These efforts aim to limit movement across multiple policy fronts. The European Union is working on multiple fronts to limit the number of Russian citizens that can enter the bloc, including the nuclear option of a total ban on all non-essential travel into the club’s Schengen zone.

articles.title: WFP warns of potential ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ as fighting blocks aid delivery
articles.summary: The UN World Food Programme warned of a humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen. Intensifying fighting has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people. Blocked roads and shifting frontlines severely restrict access to Taiz and other conflict zones. Intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people as shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restrict access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Gaza braces for winter amid attacks, joint patrols in CAR, 90 cities commit to sustainable
articles.summary: The UN and partners are preparing for winter in Gaza despite ongoing attacks on civilians. OCHA highlighted the urgent need for cold and rainy season support. Humanitarian efforts continue amid persistent violence and displacement in the territory. The UN and its partners are stepping up preparations in Gaza for the approaching cold and rainy season, even as attacks affecting civilians continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
articles.summary: The WHO reported over 125,000 suspected cholera cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The epidemic has caused 3,644 suspected deaths since January 2025. This surge occurs while the country simultaneously battles an ongoing Ebola outbreak. The cholera epidemic continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 suspected deaths were recorded between January 2025 and the end of September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Wednesday.

articles.title: Survivors Rescued From Kyiv Building After Deadly Russian Strike
articles.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv overnight, killing three people and injuring over twenty others. Survivors were rescued from a damaged building. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Western partners provided no advance warning of the attack, highlighting a gap in intelligence sharing. Moscow launched a wave of ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv overnight, killing at least three people and injuring more than 20.

articles.title: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign
articles.summary: Russia continues its aerial campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure, targeting apartment buildings, bridges, and power plants. As winter approaches, Kyiv residents are preparing for potential outages. The sustained attacks on the electricity grid aim to degrade civilian resilience during the colder months. Russia shows no sign of letting up on its escalating aerial campaign against Ukraine’s apartment buildings, bridges, power plants, electricity grid, and other targets.

articles.title: 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China
articles.summary: Satellite imagery confirms the Taliban completed a road to the China-Afghanistan border. Beijing shows no signs of opening the militarized boundary. The infrastructure project remains a dead end for trade routes. Satellite imagery sourced by RFE/RL confirms Taliban claims they have completed a road that leads up to China's remote border with Afghanistan. However there is no indication Beijing intends to open the militarized boundary any time soon.

articles.summary: नेपाल में राजदूत भर्ती प्रक्रिया में गिरि बहादुर सुनार पर यौन उत्पीड़न और 33 लाख रुपये की उगाही के आरोप लगे हैं। सऊदी अरब के लिए चुने गए इस उम्मीदवार के खिलाफ शिकायत दर्ज है। प्रधानमंत्री बालेन शाह की पारदर्शी सरकार की छवि इस घोटाले से प्रभावित हुई है। नेपाल में युवाओं के आंदोलन के बाद प्रधानमंत्री बने बालेन शाह की पारदर्शी सरकार बनाने की मुहिम विवादों में घिर गई है.

articles.title: सशस्त्र बल न्यायाधिकरण का फैसला, साथियों की पत्नियों से अवैध संबंध रखने में मेजर बर्खास्त
articles.summary: सशस्त्र बल न्यायाधिकरण ने एक मेजर को बर्खास्त कर दिया है। अदालत ने पाया कि उसने अपने साथियों की पत्नियों से अवैध संबंध बनाए रखे थे। यह फैसला सैन्य अनुशाहन के उल्लंघन के आधार पर लिया गया है। स्टीलिंग अफेक्शन: सशस्त्र बल न्यायाधिकरण का बड़ा फैसला, साथियों की पत्नियों से अवैध संबंध रखने में मेजर बर्खास्त। सशस्त्र बल न्यायाधिकरण का फैसला, साथियों की पत्नियों से अवैध संबंध रखने में मेजर बर्खास्त।
